Subject: Clarify packaging: implementation credits vs upfront fee + questions on audit logs/KMS/HSM

Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team liked the latency profile and the auditlog features. Procurement is pulling numbers together and we need a clear explanation of how Redwood structures the compliance add-ons (audit logs, KMS/HSM seats, and data residency) so we can present to finance tomorrow. Two specific asks:

1) High level packaging — options you offer for pilot -> GA (e.g., is implementation fee offset by credits, or billed upfront and amortized?). We need a simple delta: (A) Upfront implementation fee + lower recurring, or (B) Higher recurring subscription that includes an implementation credit.

2) Pricing for audit-log retention tiers and KMS/HSM seat economics — we need line items (monthly recurring vs one-time) and examples for a 12-month and 36-month term.

Also, is HIPAA residency in the US covered as a paid add-on or part of Dedicated capacity? Any SLAs we should call out?

If you can send a one-pager and a short workbook with example math, that would be great — will share with our CFO and legal (looping Kaye).

Appreciate it,

Jordan — thanks for the clear asks. I put together two packaging archetypes below and attached a short workbook with worked examples (deployment-credit-workbook.xlsx) and a draft SOW for the pilot (SOW_Draft_Greenline.pdf). Quick summary:

Option A — Upfront implementation fee (one-time) + lower recurring
- Implementation fee: $80k one-time (covers onboarding, custom connectors, evidence package)
- Recurring: base hosted API + compliance add-ons priced as line items (audit logs, KMS seat, residency surcharge)
- Credit policy: no automatic offset; we can offer a limited implementation credit applied to invoice if Greenline commits >= 12 months at a specified ARR threshold.

Option B — Amortized credit blended into subscription
- Implementation: $40k upfront + $40k as a customer credit applied monthly over 12 months (i.e., $3.33k/month)
- Recurring: slightly higher monthly ARR but lower upfront burden for procurement
- Benefits: smoother cashflow for Greenline and easier procurement approval; Redwood treats the credit as amortizable offset tied to a minimum 12-month term.

Compliance add-on pricing (examples in workbook):
- Audit logs (retention tiers): 90 days — $0.02 /GB-month; 1 year — $0.05 /GB-month; 3 years — custom pricing (volume-based; example: $0.09 /GB-month for >= 10TB)
- KMS (BYOK) seat: $750 /seat /month for managed key integration; HSM-seat (dedicated) — $2,500 /seat /month (one-time onboarding fee may apply)
- Data residency (US regions): residency surcharge 12% on base API usage for Dedicated or Private deployments; pilot can be hosted with contractual residency controls (SLA limited).

SLAs: hosted API has standard availability SLA; Dedicated/Private have an elevated SLA (we can include 99.95% uptime for Dedicated with an SLA credit schedule). HIPAA coverage: Business Associate Agreement (BAA) available; HIPAA flow-downs and breach notification terms included in the SOW.

Next steps: I recommend a short 30-minute call with Procurement + Finance + Security to walk the workbook and pick a preferred packaging. I'm available tomorrow 10–12 PT or Friday 14–16 PT.

I'll also flag finance for an amortization path if you prefer Option B; Ben, tagging you for finance/credit guidance.

Thanks,
Marissa

Marissa — quick notes from finance side before you send anything formal to Greenline:

- We should prefer Option B (partial upfront + amortized credit over 12 months) for pilots under $150k TCV — it preserves recognition and keeps cash impact manageable for customer.
- Suggest amortize credits over 12 months by default; extend to 36 months only if customer signs > 2yr committed ARR.
- For HSM-seat pricing, move to a slab model for discounts (e.g., 1 seat $2.5k/mo, 3+ seats — 10% discount). Helps when the customer asks for seat-level concessions.
- Put audit log 3-year retention as a separate procurement line item (capex-like) rather than bundling into ARR for customers wanting evidence escrow. That will avoid muddying subscription metrics.

I'll draft a short finance note for the call: "recommended amortization schedule + discount slabs". Laura — any legal redline flags on the SOW attachment?

Ben
Finance, Redwood Inference

Key attachments and links: deployment-credit-workbook.xlsx (worked 12-month and 36-month examples), SOW_Draft_Greenline.pdf (pilot onboarding + HSM onboarding clause), HubSpot deal GL-4312, drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-greenline-onboarding.

One-pager (summary):
- Preferred packaging: Option B (40/40 split) by default for pilots under $150k; monthly credit amortized over 12 months where credit is applied as invoice line item offset.
- 12-month worked example (Option B): Implementation $40k upfront, $40k credit -> $3,333/mo credit over 12 months; recurring contract $18,000/mo base ARR + $3,333 credit = net invoice show 14,667/mo for 12 months, then 18,000/mo thereafter. (Full workbook has monthly invoice lines.)
- Audit log export: standard delivery is S3 export (AES-256) on request; tamper-proofing accomplished via signed manifests and append-only write patterns; we can support third-party export for a one-time evidence fee (example in workbook).
- HSM onboarding refund: onboarding fee refundable if Redwood's integration fails to meet mutually agreed test criteria defined in the SOW (we include a 30-day remediation and acceptance test). See SOW_Draft_Greenline.pdf, §4.2 (onboarding acceptance).

Call confirmed: Fri 15:00 PT — calendar invite sent. Agenda: 1) pick packaging path; 2) go over 12-month worked math; 3) review HSM onboarding acceptance criteria; 4) next steps for SOW/PO.
